______________________________________________________________________ 
 
Old Business: 
1. Meeting Minutes – September 10, 2026  
 
Commissioner Coe moved to approve the September 10th meeting minutes. Seconded by 
Commissioner Keebler. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
2. Adoption of Findings & Decision for 217 York Street 
 
Commissioner Coe moved to adopt the findings and decisions for 217 York Street. Seconded by

Historic Preservation Commission – Meeting Minutes 
September 24th, 2026 
One Stop Home Repairs – Owner: Alan & Jessica Jansujwicz –The applicant, One 
Stop Home Repairs, requests approval for Certificate of Appropriateness for the 
replacement of 14 windows at property located at 225 Cedar Street, Map-Lot 022-057, in 
the Whitney Park Historic District. Applicant: One Stop Home Repairs. Owner: Alan & 
Jessica Jansujwicz. 
 
Chair King introduced the agenda item. 
 
Applicant Representative Howard Whelden presented on the project.  
 
HPC Consultant Pullen noted that at the pre-application meeting, the applicant stated that the windows 
would be custom made and aluminum-clad, but the current application proposes vinyl windows. Pullen 
asked why the change occurred. Applicant Representative Whelden discussed that upon looking into 
the window options, his understanding of what was available changed. Pullen asked if the applicant is 
using all vinyl – Applicant Representative Whelden confirmed.  
 
HPC Consultant Pullen asked whether the replacement windows will maintain the glass width and height 
of the existing windows, and whether infill material be needed around stock windows. Applicant 
Representative Whelden confirmed the glass will remain the same size.  
 
HPC Consultant Pullen noted that the existing 6 over 6 muntins featured narrow, putty-glazed versions. 
He asked whether the SDLs will match those details – Applicant Representative Whelden responded the 
muntin will be a half inch. 
 
HPC Consultant Pullen noted that the original windows were painted black and asked whether the new 
windows will match that color – Applicant Representative Whelden confirmed. 
 
HPC Consultant Pullen asked why the exterior trim is being replaced -- Applicant Representative 
Whelden discussed that since they are new construction windows, they have a nailing fin and require 
the trim to be removed for installation.  
 
HPC Consultant Pullen discussed a previously replaced window that had not received approval from the 
Commission, noting that it is to be included in the current project review.  
 
Chair King asked the Commission for questions. 
 
Commissioner Weitkamp asked whether the trim that is being removed is going to be replaced, and if 
so, what the details of the trim are. Applicant Representative Whelden responded that the windows have 
incorporated sills. Weitkamp asked if the height of the sill would be the same – Whelden confirmed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler asked about storm windows -- Applicant Representative Whelden responded 
that currently, there is a combination of storm windows applied to the outside, and they will not be 
included in the replacement.  
 
Chair King opened public comment – there were none. Public comment closed. 
 
Chair King asked for Commission discussion. 
 
Commissioner Keebler expressed he believes the project is appropriate and the applicant provided a 
good presentation. Commissioner Sachs agreed.
Historic Preservation Commission – Meeting Minutes 
September 24th, 2026 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commission finds the Procedural Background complete. 
Seconded by Commissioner Sachs. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1-2, the application 
satisfied Historic Preservation Code §148-9A requiring that any alteration of the historic structure will 
preserve or enhance its historical and architectural character. Seconded by Commissioner Sachs. All 
voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commission finds that Part 2, Sections 1, 5, 6, 7, 8, and Part 3, 
Sections 1-3, are not applicable. Seconded by Commissioner Weitkamp. All voting members in favor, 
none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1-2, the application 
satisfies Historic Preservation Code § 148-9B(2)(b) requiring that rehabilitation work does not destroy 
the distinguishing qualities nor character of the structure and its environment. Seconded by 
Commissioner Weitkamp. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1-2, the application 
satisfies Historic Preservation Code §148-9B(2)(c) requiring that, while repair is preferable to 
replacement, in the event that replacement of deteriorate architectural features is necessary, the feature 
being replaced in color, design, texture and other visual qualities and, where economically and 
technically feasible, materials. Seconded by Commissioner Weitkamp. All voting members in favor, 
none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1-2, the application 
satisfies Historic Preservation Code § 148-9B(2)(d) requiring that distinctive stylistic features or 
examples of skilled craftsmanship which characterize historic structures is not damaged or destroyed, 
wherever possible. Seconded by Commissioner Weitkamp. All voting members in favor, none opposed. 
Motion passed.  
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1-2, the application 
satisfies Historic Preservation Code § 148-9B(2)(i) requiring that, wherever possible, all alterations to 
structures shall be done in such a manner that if they were to be removed in the future the essential 
form and integrity of the original structure would be unimpaired. Seconded by Commissioner Weitkamp. 
All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Commissioner Keebler moved that the Commission finds that, based on the findings in Parts 1-2 of 
Section IV of this document, the Project meets the requirements for a Certificate of Appropriateness and 
therefore grants a Certificate of Appropriateness for the proposed Project. Seconded by Commissioner 
Sachs. All voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
 
Other Business: 
 
4. Open Discussion 
 
 
Chair King introduced the agenda item.  
 
Commissioner Weitkamp asked about completing more surveys of residential areas or parks near the 
old air force base – Planning Officer Collette discussed that such a project would require more funding, 
but if a grant application opens up, the project could be considered.
Historic Preservation Commission – Meeting Minutes 
September 24th, 2026 
Chair King discussed Portland’s ordinances with archaeology and concerns about metal detecting on 
City-owned and State property. Planning Officer Collette asked whether he had in mind to designate 
archaeological sites or evaluate ordinance language – King responded that it would be best to have 
ordinance language for development to consider archaeological sites and resources below ground. King 
discussed the potential of creating a plan for any below ground findings during development and when it 
may be appropriate to stop work upon findings.  
 
Chair King shared that designation of archaeological sites may create issues with looting and privacy 
and discussed potential regulations and programs for metal detectorists. Commissioner Coe 
recommended including magnet fishing with any regulations. King shared that any objects removed from 
the expedition shipwrecks are property of the United States Navy and their removal could result in 
federal penalties. Coe discussed the potential of adding signage for shipwrecks along the waterfront. 
Planning Officer Collette responded that the Parks and Recreation Department is working on creating 
signage about the history of the river and Collette had suggested that they incorporate the shipwreck 
history. Commissioner Weitkamp discussed exploring grant funding for signage of historic landmarks.  
 
HPC Consultant Pullen discussed the potential of historic brick sidewalks. Commissioner Coe discussed 
that if they were to be added, staff should consider longevity and safety.  
 
Chair King discussed the possibility of engaging Eagle Scouts and the veteran community when 
exploring signage projects. Commissioner Keebler noted the value in having a recognizable sign format 
consistent between historic signage. Commissioner Coe discussed potential opportunities to collaborate 
with local universities. Collette suggested that Commissioners could reach out to the universities to see 
if signage could be a student project. 
 
Commissioner Weitkamp asked about the process if Commissioners were to explore collaborations – 
Planning Officer Collette responded that including her on emails would be helpful. Chair King also noted 
reaching out to archaeology departments.  
 
Chair King discussed opportunities to highlight Maine Archeology Month in October and include 
information about the shipwrecks, with the caveat about restrictions on taking anything from the 
shipwrecks. 
 
The Commission selected January 21, 2027 as the next Special Meeting date. 
 
5. Adjournment 
 
Meeting adjourned at 7:49 PM.  
 
Respectfully submitted,  
 
Kayleigh Rienas 
Development Assistant

Part 1 – The Project meets the Evaluation Standards of §148-9A regarding general

1. The Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1-2, the application satisfied Historic 
Preservation Code §148-9A requiring that any alteration of the historic structure will 
preserve or enhance its historical and architectural character. 
 
Part 2 – The Project meets the Evaluation Standards of §148-9B regarding 
renovations, alterations and repairs. 
 
1. The Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1-2, the application satisfies Historic 
Preservation Code § 148-9B(2)(b) requiring that rehabilitation work does not destroy 
the distinguishing qualities nor character of the structure and its environment. 
 
2. The Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1-2, the application satisfies Historic 
Preservation Code §148-9B(2)(c) requiring that, while repair is preferable to 
replacement, in the event that replacement of deteriorated architectural features is 
necessary, the feature being replaced in color, design, texture and other visual 
qualities and, where economically and technically feasible, materials.  
 
3. The Commission finds that, based on Exhibits 1-2, the application satisfies Historic 
Preservation Code § 148-9B(2)(d) requiring that distinctive stylistic features or 
examples of skilled craftsmanship which characterize historic structures is not 
damaged or destroyed, wherever possible.

future the essential form and integrity of the original structure would be unimpaired. 
 
V. Decision 
 
The Commission finds that, based on the findings in Parts 1-2 of Section IV of this

therefore grants a Certificate of Appropriateness for the proposed Project. 
 
VI. General Permit Requirements: 
 
A. This permit does not relieve the applicant from any other state or federal permits that 
may be required for the project.  
 
B. The proposed construction, reconstruction, alteration, moving or demolition must be 
begun within 12 months of approval and completed within 24 months of approval, unless 
the Commission sets other time limits. An extension or extensions of up to one year in  
total length may be granted as a minor alteration or revision under § 148-8B.C. 
 
C. After completion of the project, or after 24 months from the issuance of a Certificate of 
Appropriateness permit, the property owner shall allow staff to access exterior areas of 
the property as reasonably necessary in order to perform an inspection to verify work 
was done in accordance with the Commission's approval. 
 
D. Any person, firm or corporation being the actual or constructive owner of any building 
or premises which is adjudged to be in violation of any of the provisions of this chapter 
shall be guilty of a civil violation and, on conviction, shall be fined not less than $10 nor 
more than $100. Each day such a violation is permitted to exist after notification shall 
constitute a separate offense. Any fines imposed pursuant to this chapter shall inure to 
the benefit of the City of Bangor. 
 
If you should have any questions or desire further information, please do not hesitate to give

The Historic Preservation Commission of the City of Bangor will hold a hearing in the Council Chambers on

application: 
 
The applicant, Blackstone Restoration, requests approval for Certificate of Appropriateness at 
property located at 28 West Broadway for the replacement of gutter lines, valleys, and downspouts. 
Additionally, the applicant proposes the replacement of the upper roof and bay window roof, as 
well as the installation of five snow guards. The project is located at 28 West Broadway, Map-Lot 
022-065, in the Whitney Park Historic District. Applicant: Blackstone Restoration. Owner: Stephen &

planning@bangormaine.gov or mail to 73 Harlow Street before 4 PM, October 7th, 2026. Interested parties
